terminal_label_correction.problem: The terminal name can be misread as evidence that multiple M11 factor dimensions mediate the head effect. The complete M11 factor rescue recovered only 0.1511 of the four-head removal effect, so the result does not support that interpretation.

valid_findings.reverse_necessity: Four-head removal recovers 0.7215 of the donor-minus-base behavior with cosine 0.9940, direction fraction 1.0, P leak 0.1186, C leak 0.00416, and positive 0.7257/0.7177 half projections.
valid_findings.complete_M11_ceiling: Restoring the entire head-induced M11 factor difference rescues only 0.1511 of the four-head removal behavior (cosine 0.9365). Therefore at least most of the measured behavior is not mediated by M11's bilinear output alone under this intervention.
valid_findings.leading_mode_within_M11: The leading occupied mode has cosine 0.9933 and signed projection 0.8738 relative to the complete M11-factor rescue. Thus it compactly describes most of the M11-local rescue vector even though that vector is a minor fraction of total behavior.
valid_findings.direct_mode_necessity: Direct leading-mode removal reaches only 0.1820 of the four-head removal effect, while remaining selective (P 0.0192, C 0.00289). This fails the registered 0.40 causal-necessity bar.

claims_forbidden: The leading occupied mode mediates most of the four-head behavioral effect.
Failure of the leading mode implies a multidimensional M11 mediator.
The M11 reader response is the only downstream use of the four-head write.
next_test: At block 11, decompose the native-donor versus head-removed output difference into the post-attention residual carrier y and the M11 output m. In a prospective 2x2 rescue factorial, add back y only, m only, or both at the block output. This directly distinguishes residual bypass, M11 mediation, and interaction before opening the complete downstream reader atlas.
